subject: Agent handshake failures after control-plane TLS rotation
messages:
From: Elaine Roberts <elaine@mediagrowth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: MediaGrowth SRE <sre@mediagrowth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent agent failures after your scheduled control-plane update

Hi Camila,

We started seeing intermittent failures from our private deployment agents at ~08:45 PT after your team’s scheduled control-plane update. Agents are dropping registration and returning handshake errors in the logs: 'tls: unknown certificate' and 'agent: heartbeat timeout'. This is affecting a handful of production pods but not the entire fleet.

Our SRE has pulled logs and we'll attach them if helpful. Can you confirm whether any TLS cert rotation, CA bundle change, or agent-side config change was applied during the update? We need an ETA on a fix — traffic is degraded for two customer-facing services.

Thanks,
Elaine Roberts
CTO, MediaGrowth

Hi Elaine — thank you for the heads-up and for the logs. I'm escalating this immediately to our infra on-call.

Short answers up front: our control plane did perform a TLS certificate rotation as part of the 08:30 upgrade window; that rotation was intended to be backward-compatible. We're investigating reports of agent handshakes rejecting the new cert chain.

Immediate next steps:
- Dev is triaging now (cc: Dev).

Subject: Re: Intermittent agent failures after your scheduled control-plane update

Hi Elaine — thanks for the logs. Quick findings from initial triage:

- The control-plane rotated its signing certificate (root CA unchanged) at 08:32. The new leaf cert uses a different SAN ordering which exposes an agent TLS verification bug in versions <= 1.4.2.
- Agents failing are on agent v1.4.2 and v1.4.1 and show the error: 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority' when verifying the server cert chain. Newer agent builds (>=1.5.0) accept the rotated chain.

Temporary mitigation (low-risk, recommended for immediate rollout):
1) On affected nodes, restart the Redwood agent process to force re-negotiation (kubectl rollout restart daemonset/redwood-agent).
2) If restarts are not feasible, add the control-plane intermediate cert to the agent container trust store at /etc/ssl/certs/redwood-intermediate.pem and SIGHUP the agent process.

We are preparing a backpatch for agent v1.4.x to accept the rotated chain; ETA for the patched agent image is ~6 hours. In parallel, we will push an emergency revert of the leaf cert rotation if the mitigations do not reduce impact.

I’ve attached a short mitigation checklist and a CSV with heartbeat metrics for your fleet slice. Please apply step 1 on a canary pod and report results.

—Dev Patel
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Dev — we applied the daemonset restart to a 5-node canary group and two of the restarted agents re-registered successfully; three still showed the TLS error. Attached is a filtered log bundle from one failing node.

Impact: ~8% of our production traffic is currently routed to degraded pods. Our on-call wants a firm ETA on the patched agent image or the cert revert; if the revert is required we need that communicated to procurement as it may affect change windows on our side.

Also — please document whether this requires us to change any local trust bundles long-term; we prefer not to modify node-level CA stores unless absolutely necessary.

—Elaine

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Root cause, short-term remediation, and follow-up actions — MediaGrowth private deployment incident

Elaine and team — apologies again for the disruption. Summarizing the outcome and our follow-ups so you have a single record: 

Root cause (postmortem summary):
- The control-plane leaf certificate was rotated in the 08:30 upgrade window. The new certificate chain included an intermediate certificate presented in an order that triggered a parsing-verification path in agent code v1.4.x that incorrectly rejected a valid chain.
- Agents running v1.5.0+ were unaffected. The failure manifested as agent registration handshake timeouts and x509 verification errors.

Short-term remediation completed: 
- We recommended a controlled daemonset restart for agents; that restored ~60% of affected agents.
- We released an emergency backported agent image (v1.4.3-patch1) addressing the verification bug. You were notified of the image at 11:02 PT on 11/03.
- Where immediate restarts were not possible, we coordinated a targeted cert re-presentation from the control plane to the agents; that lowered error rates in your remaining nodes.

Longer-term actions (commitments):
- Release schedule: All private clusters will receive an agent auto-update that includes the fix over the next 72 hours; we will provide a staged rollout plan and will not auto-upgrade outside agreed maintenance windows for MediaGrowth without explicit signoff.
- Hardening: additional unit tests around cert chain ordering and integration tests in our upgrade pipeline.
- Incident artifacts: full postmortem doc and logs shared to the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/MediaGrowth-incident-20261103 and ticket INF-4921.
- Credits: per our escalation policy, we will issue a service credit for the degraded period; my team will follow up with procurement to include the formal credit calculation.

Attachments included: mitigation-checklist.pdf, controlplane-heartbeat-metrics.csv, server-logs.tar.gz (from your upload).

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute bridge next week to walk through the postmortem and rollout plan. Please let me know availability.

Thanks for the patience and for working through the mitigations with us.

—Camila Reyes
